question: Whether the filing-fee rule under Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 applies to, or otherwise determines the fee for, relief under §§ 9-11-15(3) and 21-23-7(6).
whyItIsOpen: Section 99-19-72 levies a $150 filing fee on 'each petition to expunge an offense under Section 99-19-71', to be collected by the circuit clerk. Sections 9-11-15(3) and 21-23-7(6) sit outside § 99-19-71 and neither specifies a fee of its own, so the fee does not reach them by the statute's terms. The collection mechanism also names the circuit clerk, which does not map onto a petition filed in justice or municipal court. Neither point is settled on the face of the statute, and construing it either way would be legal research this record does not perform.

feeOrWaiverQuestion: Two questions, and both must be answered before any fee is published on this track. First: what filing fee, if any, does each receiving court charge for the petition — the § 99-19-72 figure, a local figure, or none. Second: what waiver route exists, whether a pauper's affidavit is accepted, and on what form.
receivingCourtDistinction: The two branches are separate contracts filed in different courts before different prosecutors, and they may carry different fees. The justice-court branch under § 9-11-15(3) is filed with the clerk of the justice court of conviction. The municipal-court branch under § 21-23-7(6) is filed with the clerk of the municipal court of conviction, with notice to the municipal prosecuting attorney. A fee confirmed for one branch may not be assumed for the other, and neither may be assumed from the circuit-court figure in § 99-19-72.
legalEscalationIfSilentOrConflicting: If the AOC publishes no statewide figure and the clerks of the two courts give no written instruction, or if a clerk instruction conflicts with § 99-19-72 on its face, the question escalates to counsel as a genuine question of statutory reach: whether § 99-19-72 levies its fee on a petition brought under a section other than § 99-19-71 and filed in a court other than circuit court. It does not escalate merely because a source has not yet been retrieved — an unacquired source is an acquisition task, not a legal question.
interimProductTreatment: The packet publishes no fee amount on this track and instructs the participant to confirm the filing fee, and any pauper's-affidavit route, with the clerk of the court before filing. That is the treatment already recorded in the memo and it remains correct while this is open.
